Description: An Optimistic Rollup executing transactions off Ethereum L1 and settling state roots back to Ethereum using fraud proofs and a challenge window.
Reason for inclusion: Defines and operates a production Optimistic Rollup with custom fraud-proof logic, sequencer execution rules, and Ethereum-anchored settlement contracts.
Protocol & Security: Optimistic Rollup secured by Ethereum with interactive fraud proofs and a fixed challenge window; correctness enforced via dispute resolution on L1.
Execution Model: Single sequencer executes transactions off-chain; batches posted to Ethereum with EVM-equivalent execution.
Settlement & Finality: State roots settled optimistically to Ethereum; finality achieved after challenge window expiration.
Governance & Control: Protocol upgrades and parameters governed by Arbitrum DAO with multisig safeguards.
Ecosystem Signals (non-app-specific): High TVL concentration, sustained transaction throughput, broad developer adoption across DeFi and infra.
Protocol Ownership: Core protocol maintained by Offchain Labs; governed by Arbitrum DAO with onchain voting and multisigs.
Research & Roadmap: Focused on fraud-proof decentralization, permissionless validation, and sequencer decentralization.
Operational Risk: Single-sequencer reliance; complexity of dispute system; governance coordination risk.
Framework Architecture: Built on Arbitrum Nitro optimistic execution framework.
Deployment Model: Single canonical rollup network; Nitro also supports additional Arbitrum chains.
Interoperability: Ethereum-native settlement; interoperability primarily via bridges and messaging layers outside the protocol.
Practitioner’s note: Arbitrum prioritizes high throughput and EVM equivalence, with a complex but mature dispute system. Sequencer decentralization and fraud-proof participation remain active areas of evolution.
Practitioner validation check: If Arbitrum were removed, Ethereum would lose a live optimistic execution environment with its own fraud-proof rules and settlement guarantees.

Description: An Optimistic Rollup protocol executing transactions off-chain and relying on fraud proofs with a defined challenge period for Ethereum settlement.
Reason for inclusion: Maintains the OP Stack and governs optimistic execution rules, fraud-proof architecture, and sequencing assumptions used in production on mainnet.
Protocol & Security: Optimistic Rollup using fraud proofs and Ethereum L1 settlement; security assumptions defined by OP Stack contracts.
Execution Model: Sequencer-based off-chain execution with EVM equivalence; standardized execution via OP Stack.
Settlement & Finality: Optimistic settlement to Ethereum with a challenge period before finality.
Governance & Control: Governed by Optimism Collective (Token House + Citizens’ House); protocol evolution coordinated across OP Stack ecosystem.
Ecosystem Signals (non-app-specific): Strong developer momentum; expanding Superchain ecosystem; growing OP Stack adoption.
Protocol Ownership: Maintained by Optimism Foundation and governed by the Optimism Collective.
Research & Roadmap: Standardization of optimistic rollups, Superchain interoperability, and fault-proof maturity.
Operational Risk: Shared framework risk across OP Stack chains; sequencer centralization in early stages.
Framework Architecture: Canonical implementation of the OP Stack framework.
Deployment Model: Single rollup plus governance-aligned Superchain members.
Interoperability: Designed for Superchain-level coordination; external interoperability handled via bridges.
Practitioner’s note: Optimism emphasizes simplicity, modularity, and ecosystem standardization. Its influence extends beyond a single chain via the OP Stack.
Practitioner validation check: If Optimism were removed, a widely adopted optimistic execution standard and its fraud-proof model would cease to exist on Ethereum.

Description: A production Optimistic Rollup built on the OP Stack, executing transactions off L1 and settling to Ethereum via optimistic assumptions.
Reason for inclusion: Operates a canonical Optimistic Rollup mainnet that inherits and enforces OP Stack fraud-proof logic and challenge rules in production.
Protocol & Security: Inherits OP Stack optimistic security model with fraud proofs and Ethereum settlement; no custom security logic.
Execution Model: Centralized sequencer executing OP Stack transactions off-chain.
Settlement & Finality: State commitments posted to Ethereum; finality after OP Stack challenge window.
Governance & Control: Operated by Coinbase; protocol rules inherited from OP Stack governance rather than Base-specific governance.
Ecosystem Signals (non-app-specific): High user onboarding via Coinbase distribution; strong retail transaction volume.
Protocol Ownership: Operated by Coinbase; protocol rules inherited from OP Stack governance.
Research & Roadmap: Aligned with OP Stack roadmap; minimal independent protocol research.
Operational Risk: Operator centralization; dependency on OP Stack upgrades.
Interoperability: Ethereum-native; interoperates through standard bridge infrastructure.
Practitioner’s note: Base does not define new optimistic mechanics but is a critical real-world implementation testing optimistic rollups at scale under a centralized operator.
Practitioner validation check: If Base were removed, OP Stack optimistic execution would lose a major production deployment validating its assumptions under heavy usage.
